source.locator: Section 3 and the online supplement's superpopulation asymptotics for factorial-IV cell means, ratios, Wald inference, and Fieller inversion

attestation.note: A stable DOI is supplied because the frozen core contains no lawful verbatim transcription; the locator records the published asymptotic result used here.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the coordinate-separable family definition to establish the exact separable and interactive counts.

proposed.justification: The exact count and the six fully interactive maps show that the admissible relaxation is substantively larger than coordinate-specific receipt.
proposed.gap: No inspected paper gives a symbolic three-factor WARP classification subject to simultaneous zero-Möbius restrictions.
proposed.consumer: The theorem provides a finite, interpretable compliance menu for \(\texttt{factiv::iv\_factorial}\) users and the New Haven factorial-IV analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The identifying equalities require the maintained response support to lie in the stated model class and use the Möbius signature definition explicitly.

proposed.justification: The formulas translate the behavioral envelope into estimands computable from randomized assignment cells.
proposed.gap: The signed ratios coincide algebraically with existing perfect-complier formulas under separable receipt; the new claim is their validity on the strictly larger classified envelope.
proposed.consumer: The result directly supplies all seven main and interaction effects required by a three-factor perfect-complier analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The explicit countermodel proof directly uses full assignment support, one-sided rational support, the separable maps, and the null-envelope definition.

proposed.justification: Complete equality of the observed law rules out reliance on a failed diagnostic moment and certifies outcome-nonrestrictive maximality.
proposed.gap: Goff's row-space converse implies nonidentification abstractly; the proposed subset-inversion witness is explicit for every excluded rational addition and preserves nondegenerate Bernoulli outcomes.
proposed.consumer: The countermodels prevent researchers from interpreting signed ratios after adding any behavior outside the envelope, even when first-stage diagnostics happen to cancel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The equivalence proof consumes the signed-identification theorem for sufficiency and the explicit maximal-converse theorem for necessity.

proposed.justification: The iff statement identifies the largest economically rational relaxation rather than offering another sufficient compliance restriction.
proposed.gap: Blackwell--Pashley impose coordinate-specific receipt, while Goff supplies a generic criterion and a two-factor boundary rather than this three-factor maximal support.
proposed.consumer: The theorem tells factorial-IV analysts exactly which interactive uptake behaviors leave every perfect-complier factorial estimand intact.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof invokes the published finite-cell central-limit, delta-method, covariance-consistency, and Wald result recorded as a cited leaf.

proposed.justification: All effects share signed cell moments and denominators, so joint covariance propagation is necessary for simultaneous claims.
proposed.gap: Blackwell--Pashley provide the scalar and vector factorial-IV ingredients; this theorem records their adaptation to the Möbius vector and is an inference rung rather than the novelty kernel.
proposed.consumer: The result permits family-wise statements about all seven factorial effects in software and applied reanalysis when the perfect-complier share is not weak.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof invokes the published studentized finite-cell moment limit recorded as a cited leaf before applying the finite Bonferroni union bound.

proposed.justification: Test inversion remains informative about identification weakness because it is allowed to return unbounded sets.
proposed.gap: Existing factorial-IV work treats scalar Fieller intervals; the contribution here is the explicit Bonferroni product and Walsh image for the dependent eight-ratio system, not uniform weak-share adaptation.
proposed.consumer: Applied analysts obtain a simultaneous fallback when the estimated perfect-complier share is too small for the Wald ellipsoid.
